Celxpert Energy.why: Taiwanese lithium-ion battery-pack maker developing BBU / UPS backup batteries: its BBU roadmap targets product certification in 2026H1, pilot run and sample shipments in 2026H2 and mass production in 2027, with line expansion for BBU and an ESS/BBU/Other 2027 target of 35% of its product mix
Celxpert Energy.evidence: Celxpert Energy IR presentation: MOPS 332320251230E001 (12-30-2025): 'Backup Power: UPS BBU - Uninterrupted backup power to prevent data loss or system downtime during power outages'; Outlook: 'BBU: Certification targeted for 1H26; sample shipments to begin 2H26.'

players.product: Lithium-ion battery packs (notebook, network, power tool, e-bike, drone) and energy storage systems; BBU / UPS backup batteries in development (certification targeted 1H26, pilot run and sample shipments 2H26, mass production 2027)

quarterly_data.signal: BBU development roadmap: end of 2025 - optimization and internal validation (continue functional and reliability testing; complete key internal validation to prepare for mass production); 2026H1 - product certification based on customer and market requirements, preparing for subsequent mass production; 2026H2 - pilot run and sample shipments (begin pilot production and deliver samples to customers for validation tests); 2027 - official transition to mass production, with customer shipments ramping up as demand increases. Outlook slide: 'BBU: Certification targeted for 1H26; sample shipments to begin 2H26.'

Energy Storage & BBU: company says pull-in momentum remains limited with most programs under planning / adjustment; technical groundwork and project deployments are in place, with recovery expected from 2026, 'positioning these segments as key mid-to-long-term growth drivers.' The company is focusing on high-value product lines: E-Bike, BBU and drones.

Target product mix: non-3C products to reach 50%-55% of revenue in 2026. Product mix chart (2024Y / 2025Q1~Q3 / 2027 targets, as printed): NB 67% / 62% / 40%; Network 9% / 8% / 10%; Power Tool 17% / 19% / 18%; E-Mobility 5% / 4% / 10%; Drone 2% (2025Q1~Q3) / 10% (2027 target); ESS/BBU/Other 2% / 5% / 35%.
quarterly_data.figure: non-3C products 50%-55% of 2026 revenue; ESS/BBU/Other 35% 2027 target (5% in 2025Q1~Q3)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity expansion and automation for 2026-2027 scaling: a new plant in Taiwan is planned in 2026 to upgrade capacity; line expansion for BBU, drones and E-Bike; automation rollout across Taiwan and China plants to enhance efficiency. Sites shown: Celxpert Headquarter, Celxpert Kunshan and Celxpert Nantong (planning).

Consolidated revenue for January-September 2025 was NT$3.843 billion, down 6.05% YoY, which the company attributes to softer market demand and product mix adjustments; it says core customer relationships remain stable and new product / application development continues. 2025Q1-3 (NT$ million): net revenue 3,843 (2024Q1-3: 4,091; -6%), gross profit 302 (7.9%), loss from operations 151 (3.9%), net loss 140, loss attributable to owners of parent 149, basic EPS -NT$1.58. 2025 3Q: net revenue 1,375 (2024 3Q: 1,449; -5%), gross profit 122 (8.9%), loss from operations 41 (3.0%), net loss 25, basic EPS -NT$0.26.
quarterly_data.figure: January-September 2025 revenue NT$3.843 billion, -6.05% YoY; 2025 3Q revenue NT$1,375 million, -5% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Segment review: Notebook - shipments remained relatively stable; new models were impacted by customer procurement strategy shifts and China localization trends; product integration and differentiated design are being strengthened, with benefits expected to materialize gradually from 2026. Network - legacy model demand declined; new models are in early ramp-up and process adjustment, with capacity and process optimization largely in place to support future volume scaling. Power Tools - geopolitical and macro uncertainty weighed on end-market demand; the company is sustaining core accounts and developing new customers. E-Bikes - end-market softness and customer inventory digestion delayed new product schedules to late 2025; momentum is expected to recover as channel inventory normalizes.

Outlook ('Operations Stabilizing; Transformation Taking Hold'): Notebook & Power Tool - actively developing new customers, more than two accounts currently under negotiation; Network - steady demand growth from existing customers, 2-3 new projects awarded; E-Bike - two new international brands secured in addition to existing clients, shipments expected 2026 Q2; LEV (golf carts / forklifts) - entering the light EV market, shipments expected 2026 Q1; Drones - stable shipments to existing clients, two new awarded projects. New applications: gradual expansion into AGV and robotics as mid- to long-term growth drivers.
quarterly_data.figure: Network 2-3 new projects awarded; E-Bike shipments expected 2026 Q2; LEV shipments expected 2026 Q1

quarterly_data.signal: Company profile: >20 years of experience in manufacturing and designing Li-ion batteries, >2000 employees, >USD 400 millions revenue. Products: battery packs for notebooks and tablet PCs, modems, smartphones and networking, power tools, gardening tools and vacuum cleaners; solar street lighting storage; energy storage systems (lithium batteries integrated with battery management, temperature regulation and system controllers, for reliable power management and smart grid operations); backup power UPS / BBU (uninterrupted backup power to prevent data loss or system downtime during power outages); e-mobility (e-motor, electric forklift, electric scissor lift, e-bike); drones. Company-cited strengths: professional battery pack design and test capability, an independent safety laboratory, more than 20 years of battery management system design, self-developed test equipment and automated production.
